items.title: 70980_Quinn Wilson oral history interview
items.q: Well, I was recommended by Franz Jackson. They were looking for a bass player for a New Year's Eve gig, and they wanted a tuba player, and they didn't know any other tuba players, so they wanted to get Franz Jackson's tuba player, and Franz Jackson said, 'I don't lend my tuba player out to anybody.

ctx.x: You've got beautiful, beautiful teeth. Look like they're just made for a brass instrument. Probably helped do it.

The funny part about it, though, was when Franz Jackson recommended me to Bill -- Ruth and Bill Reinhart (PHONETIC), come in on tuba. I hadn't played it then in about -- that's about three or four years. It was longer than that since I played Dixieland. So she said, well, you think you can make it? I said, oh, yeah, I can make it. So what I did was I got all different records, played along with the phonograph to try to see if I had that swing beat again. Come to find out, I said, yeah, I can play all the tunes…
On New Year's Eve. For a one-night gig. Wound up 12 years at Jazz Limited.
